transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... lately I've been trying to clean up my image and my daily routine for some arts board stuff I'm involved with. But ever since I started doing that, I've just been a lot more tense and down than I expected to be. 

I mean, I'm still doing the basics and getting by, but I keep dropping these little things that I normally really care about—like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then... I just feel guilty about falling behind, so I end up canceling plans with people instead of actually catching up on the things I missed. It's just been getting to me, so I figured I should come in.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you normally like to do, or has that changed recently?

Um, I haven't really noticed a change there. I think I still enjoy the things I usually like doing. It's not really that I don't like them anymore... it's more just that I get too caught up feeling guilty about my schedule to actually go out and do them right now. But when I do, it's still fun.
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable, but now feel empty or unenjoyable when you do them?

No, not really. Like I said, I still enjoy things when I actually do them. It's just the guilt and the stress of falling behind that gets in the way of starting them, but the things themselves haven't lost their appeal or anything.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Um, no, not really. I don't feel anxious or worried most of the time. It's just... like I said, mostly just the stress and guilt about not getting my stuff done for the board. But I wouldn't say I feel anxious in general.
Do you feel sad most of the day?
No, I don't think so. I wouldn't say I feel sad. It's really just the frustration with myself over the schedule, but I don't feel down or sad during the day.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um, I'd say it's been going on for about two months now. It pretty much started right when I began trying to overhaul my routine and my presentation.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still enjoy the things I normally like to do. It's really just the stress about my routine and the presentation that's bothering me, but I still care about my hobbies and everything else just the same.
Do you feel like you're not looking forward to things that you normally would?

No, not really. I still look forward to doing things I normally enjoy. Like I was saying, it's really just this specific stress with my routine and the presentation hanging over my head. But outside of that, I still get excited for normal stuff.
Do you feel like you have less energy than you used to?

No, my energy is fine. I don't feel any more tired or drained than usual. It's really just the mental stress of trying to get this presentation and routine figured out, but physically, my energy levels haven't really changed at all.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
No, I haven't noticed any changes with my weight. It's been pretty much the exact same as it always is.
Do you find yourself getting irritable or short-tempered more often than you used to?

No, not really. I haven't been snapping at anyone or feeling extra irritable. It's just... I'm stressed about the presentation, but it hasn't made me short-tempered or anything like that. I'm pretty much my usual self when it comes to my mood.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight unintentionally since you started feeling stressed about your routine and presentation?
No, like I just mentioned, my weight hasn't changed at all. I definitely haven't lost any weight, unintentionally or otherwise. It's stayed exactly the same.
Do you often feel worthless or guilty about things beyond just your schedule and presentation?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel bad that I'm struggling so much right now with this one thing, but I wouldn't say I feel worthless. And I don't really feel guilty about anything else going on in my life. It's really just the stress from this whole presentation thing.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of stress and guilt for most of every day?

Well, like I said, I don't really have those feelings of guilt. But as for the stress... no, it's not most of every day. 

I mean, it definitely hits me when I'm actively thinking about the presentation or trying to figure out my schedule. But if I'm doing something else or just distracted, I feel fine. So it's not really a constant, all-day kind of thing.
For how long have you been feeling down or frustrated about your schedule and presentation?
It's been about two months. That's really when all this started, right when I decided to try and completely overhaul my routine and work on this presentation.
Would you say that these feelings of stress and frustration have been mild, or have they been more significant and impacting your daily life?

I'd say it's more on the mild side, honestly. I'm still getting through my basic errands and everyday commitments just fine. It's not stopping me from functioning completely. But... I have noticed I'm a lot less reliable lately with the things people usually count on me for. Like, I volunteer with fair planning, and I do some design work, and I've just been really dropping the ball on following through with those. So it's affecting things, just not everything.
Would you say these feelings of stress and frustration have interfered with your social or occupational functioning to a significant degree?

I wouldn't say it's to a significant degree, no. Um... like I just mentioned, I'm still managing my day-to-day life okay. I'm not working right now, so there's no job for it to interfere with, and socially things are mostly fine. 

It's really just those specific volunteer commitments where I'm falling behind. So... yeah, it's definitely not completely derailing my life or anything.
Would you describe your recent feelings of stress and frustration as causing you significant distress?

No, I wouldn't call it significant distress. I mean, it's annoying and I'm definitely frustrated with myself for not sticking to the schedule I made, but it's not like... overwhelming me or keeping me up at night. It's just a mild frustration that I can't seem to get my act together with this one project.
